components.summary: A code diff in unified or split layout with syntax highlighting, folding, line selection and annotations.

types.name: DiffView
types.doc: Draws the [`DiffState`] an app keeps in its state: give it the state's accessors and build it in the view. It fills the height it's given and scrolls; Cmd-C, `j`/`k` and `]`/`[` work once the app routes keys to [`DiffState::key`].  ```ignore DiffView::new(|s: &App| &s.diff, |s: &mut App| &mut s.diff) .annotation(|s: &App, a: &Annotation| comment(s, &a.id)) .on_comment(|s: &mut App, lines, _| s.compose(lines)) .on_visible_file(|s: &mut App, f| s.tree.reveal(f)) .build(s, &k) ```

methods.name: new
methods.sig: fn new(get: impl Fn(&S) -> &DiffState + 'static, get_mut: impl Fn(&mut S) -> &mut DiffState + 'static) -> DiffView<S>

methods.name: key
methods.sig: fn key(self, key: impl Into<String>) -> Self
methods.doc: The view's element key (`"diff"` by default); give each diff in a window its own.

methods.name: fold_row
methods.doc: How folded unchanged lines draw: [`FoldRow::Summary`] by default, or Pierre's [`FoldRow::LineInfo`] as OpenCode Desktop's review has them.

methods.name: annotation
methods.sig: fn annotation(self, f: impl Fn(&S, &Annotation) -> El + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Build each [`Annotation`] under its line. Rows holding annotations are built every commit, so a widget can read app state (a composer's text) freely.

methods.name: header_actions
methods.sig: fn header_actions(self, f: impl Fn(&S, usize) -> El + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Extra controls at the end of each file's header (a "viewed" toggle, a menu), by file.

methods.name: on_select
methods.sig: fn on_select(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, Option<LineRange>, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called when a click, shift-click or drag on the line numbers ends, with the selection.

methods.name: on_comment
methods.sig: fn on_comment(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, LineRange, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Show a "+" by the line numbers of the hovered line, and call `f` with the lines it stands for when pressed: the selection when the line is in it, else that line.

methods.name: on_visible_file
methods.sig: fn on_visible_file(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called when the file at the top of the view changes as it scrolls, to follow it in a file tree.

types.name: DiffState
types.doc: A diff and everything about how it is shown: the app keeps one in its state and [`DiffView`](super::DiffView) draws it.

methods.name: set_files
methods.doc: Show `files` instead, every range collapsed again and the selection cleared. Annotations stay; drop or remap them with [`DiffState::set_annotations`].

methods.name: file_index
methods.doc: The index of the file at `path` (its new path, or old for a deleted file).

methods.name: set_mode
methods.doc: Switch between unified and split. Rows keep their keys where they can (unchanged and removed lines), so a switch made in a handler that calls `Tx::motion` springs them to their new places.

methods.name: single_column
methods.doc: In split mode, the one side `file` shows across the whole width, as a single column: an added file's new side or a deleted file's old side ([`FileDiff::sole_side`]). `None` in unified mode and for a file with both sides.

methods.name: set_wrap
methods.doc: Wrap long lines (rows grow), or keep them on one line and scroll sideways (the default). Split wraps either way, as side-by-side review does, so both sides stay in view.

methods.name: set_highlighter
methods.doc: Highlight code with `h` instead of the built-in highlighter.

methods.name: set_collapsed
methods.sig: fn set_collapsed(&self, file: usize, collapsed: bool)
methods.doc: Show only `file`'s header, or its lines again.

methods.name: hidden
methods.sig: fn hidden(&self, file: usize, gap: usize) -> Option<u32>
methods.doc: Lines of `file`'s unchanged range before hunk `gap` still hidden, when known.

methods.name: expand
methods.sig: fn expand(&self, file: usize, gap: usize, how: Expand)
methods.doc: Reveal more of `file`'s unchanged range before hunk `gap` (`hunks.len()`: after the last). Does nothing without the file's whole text.

methods.name: set_annotations
methods.doc: Show these annotations under their lines, in order where several share a line.

methods.name: selected_text
methods.doc: The selected lines' text on the side the selection started on, one per line, without numbers or markers: what copying the selection gives.

methods.name: scroll_to_file
methods.sig: fn scroll_to_file(&self, file: usize, tx: &mut Tx)
methods.doc: Scroll `file`'s header to the top.

methods.name: scroll_to_line
methods.sig: fn scroll_to_line(&self, file: usize, at: LineRef, tx: &mut Tx)
methods.doc: Scroll to `file`'s line `at`, opening the range it's in if it's hidden, and put it below the header.

methods.name: next_hunk
methods.sig: fn next_hunk(&self, forward: bool, tx: &mut Tx) -> bool
methods.doc: Bring the next (or previous) hunk to just below the sticky header.

methods.name: next_file
methods.sig: fn next_file(&self, forward: bool, tx: &mut Tx) -> bool
methods.doc: Scroll to the next (or previous) file's header.

methods.name: key
methods.sig: fn key(&self, ev: &KeyEvent, tx: &mut Tx) -> bool
methods.doc: Handle a key for the diff: `j`/`k` next and previous hunk, `]`/`[` next and previous file, Escape clears the line selection, Cmd-C copies it, and Shift (with `App::modifier_keys`) makes a click on a line number extend the selection. Call it from the app's `on_key`; it returns whether it took the key.

types.name: DiffMode
types.doc: How a diff lays out its two sides.

variants.name: Unified
variants.doc: One column, removed lines above the added lines that replace them.

variants.name: Split
variants.doc: Old on the left, new on the right, changed lines side by side. An added or deleted file shows its one side as a single column.

types.name: FileDiff
types.doc: One file's changes.

methods.name: from_texts
methods.sig: fn from_texts(path: impl Into<String>, old: &str, new: &str) -> FileDiff
methods.doc: The diff of `old` to `new`, a file at `path`, with three lines of context around each change and word changes on paired lines. Both texts stay with it, so every unchanged range between hunks can be expanded.

methods.name: from_texts_with_context
methods.sig: fn from_texts_with_context(path: impl Into<String>, old: &str, new: &str, context: u32) -> FileDiff
methods.doc: [`FileDiff::from_texts`] with `context` unchanged lines around each change instead of three: four is what jsdiff (and so OpenCode Desktop) keeps.

methods.name: between
methods.sig: fn between(old_path: Option<String>, new_path: Option<String>, old: &str, new: &str) -> FileDiff
methods.doc: [`FileDiff::from_texts`] for a file whose path changed (a rename), was added (`old_path` `None`, `old` empty) or deleted (`new_path` `None`, `new` empty).

methods.name: between_with_context
methods.sig: fn between_with_context(old_path: Option<String>, new_path: Option<String>, old: &str, new: &str, context: u32) -> FileDiff
methods.doc: [`FileDiff::between`] with `context` unchanged lines around each change.

methods.name: path
methods.doc: The path to show: the new one, or the old one for a deleted file.

methods.name: additions
methods.doc: Lines added.

methods.name: deletions
methods.doc: Lines removed.

methods.name: language
methods.doc: The highlighter language for the path, as Desktop names it from the file name ([`lang_for_path`](crate::syntax::lang_for_path)): `"rust"`, `"tsx"`, `"makefile"`.

methods.name: expandable
methods.doc: Whether the unchanged lines between hunks can be shown.

methods.name: sole_side
methods.doc: The only side the file has: `New` for an added file, `Old` for a deleted one, `None` when it has both. A file diffed from texts counts as added when its old text is empty and its new one isn't (and the other way round as deleted), unless it moved.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The whole text of `side`, when the diff has it ([`FileDiff::from_texts`], [`FileDiff::fold`]).

methods.name: fold
methods.doc: A diff whose one hunk holds the whole file, as a patch made with full context does, folded as a diff of the two texts is: the hunk splits around its changes with `context` unchanged lines each side, and the texts it holds stay with the diff, so every folded range can be expanded. The lines pair as they did in the patch. A diff of any other shape (more than one hunk, or one that starts past the first line) comes back as it was.

types.name: FileStatus
types.doc: What happened to a file.

types.name: Annotation
types.doc: A widget the app shows under a line, such as a review comment or a composer. The app builds it from `id` (see [`DiffView::annotation`](super::DiffView::annotation)).

types.name: LineRange
types.doc: Selected lines of one file, from where the selection started to where it ends (either way round), as a click, shift-click or drag down the line numbers makes them.

methods.name: line

methods.doc: One line.

types.doc: Which way an unchanged range between hunks opens.

components.name: Markdown
components.summary: Renders Markdown, including streaming text, tables, code blocks with syntax highlighting, find highlights and selection.

types.name: Markdown
types.doc: Markdown source as an element. See the module docs for cost and keys.

methods.name: find
methods.sig: fn find(src: &str, query: &str, case: Case) -> Vec<Vec<Range<usize>>>
methods.doc: Finds non-overlapping matches of `query` in the rendered text of `src` (see [`find`]).

methods.name: images
methods.sig: fn images(self, f: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Image> + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: The picture for an image's source as written (`![alt](src)`): a decoded or decoding [`Image`] from the app's cache, or `None` when it has none. Until it decodes, and without one, the image shows Chromium's broken-image glyph and its alt text, as a web page does for an `` with no picture. Without this, every image does.

methods.name: image_frame
methods.sig: fn image_frame(self, f: impl Fn(El, &ImageFrame<'_>) -> El + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Draws `f(image, frame)` in place of each image that shows its picture, so an app can open it larger on a press (`markdown.css`'s `cursor: zoom-in`, a button named by its alt text) or key it for a flight into a viewer.

methods.name: link_favicon
methods.sig: fn link_favicon(self, f: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<Pixels> + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: The image to draw before a link to `url` in place of [`MarkdownStyle::link_icons`]' globe: the site's favicon, once the app has fetched and decoded it (`None` until then, and for sites it won't ask). GitHub links keep GitHub's mark.

methods.name: on_link
methods.sig: fn on_link<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called with a link's destination when it is clicked, or pressed with Enter or Space while focused. With a handler, links show a hand and a solid underline under the pointer and are Tab stops; without one they are styled text only. Shares its slot with [`Self::on_link_tx`] (the later call wins).

methods.name: on_link_tx
methods.sig: fn on_link_tx<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: [`Self::on_link`] with the [`Tx`] of the press, for a handler that opens a screen, scrolls or copies in the same commit (an app's own `scheme:id` links, say). Replaces any earlier `on_link` or `on_link_tx` handler (the later call wins).

methods.name: on_link_secondary
methods.sig: fn on_link_secondary<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, PointerPress, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called with a link's destination and the point (window points) when a right-click (or macOS control-click) lands on it: a menu for that link (Open, Copy Link). It takes the press from the menus of the elements around the Markdown, which still get right-clicks elsewhere in the text. Links show a hand and are Tab stops with this alone, too.

methods.name: link_style
methods.sig: fn link_style(self, f: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<(Span, LinkPaint)> + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: A look for some links by destination. `f` returns `None` for the default look ([`MarkdownStyle::link`] with its underline, and an accent underline on hover), or `Some((resting, hover))`: the [`Span`] drawn over the link's text (colour, weight, `bg` with its padding, underline; its range is ignored, and emphasis, strong and inline code inside the link keep their styles over it) and the [`LinkPaint`] over it while hovered. Applies with or without a handler.

methods.name: link_ring
methods.sig: fn link_ring(self, f: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<(Color, f32)> + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: An inset border ring `(color, width_pt)` inside the rounded [`Span::bg`] of chosen links by destination (`None`: no ring). Stays on hover unless the link's hover [`LinkPaint`] sets its own [`LinkPaint::ring`]. Applies with or without a handler. Links without a background draw no resting ring; use [`Self::link_style`] to set one.

methods.name: link_help
methods.sig: fn link_help(self, f: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String> + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: A tooltip for links by destination (`None`: none), shown after the hover delay while the pointer rests on the link ([`Link::help`]): where it goes, say. Links take it only with a handler ([`Self::on_link`] or [`Self::on_link_secondary`]).

methods.name: highlights
methods.sig: fn highlights(self, highlights: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl HighlightItem>) -> Self
methods.doc: Highlight UTF-8 byte ranges of the Markdown source string (see [`find`]).  Ranges refer to the source passed to [`Markdown::new`] (as `pulldown_cmark`'s offset iterator reports them) and map across inline formatting, code blocks, headings, lists, blockquotes and tables without reshaping text or shifting layout. Each highlight is reachable by [`Tx::scroll_into_view`](rune::Tx::scroll_into_view) and [`Cx::layout`](rune::Cx::layout) under its [`Highlight::key`], or under [`Markdown::highlight_key`]`(i)` when no key was set on it. Backgrounds, rings and foreground colours are paint-only. Matches add no layout nodes; [`Runtime::elements`](rune::Runtime::elements) reports a `mark` per rendered fragment. Empty/out-of-source ranges paint nothing; partial UTF-8 characters expand to boundaries.  ```ignore let view = Markdown::new(src).highlights(markdown::find(src, query, Case::Insensitive)).build(&kit); ```

methods.name: highlight_key
methods.doc: Default key (`"md-mark-{index}"`) for the `index`-th highlight in [`Self::highlights`] when [`Highlight::key`] was not set on it.

methods.name: autolink
methods.doc: Whether bare `https://…`, `http://…` and `www.…` URLs in plain text are autolinked (`true` by default). This is URL-only: bare email addresses remain text; `<name@example.org>` still links.

methods.name: block_keys
methods.sig: fn block_keys<I, K>(self, keys: I) -> Self
methods.doc: Stable keys as `(source_byte_offset, key)` pairs. The offset is the start of the first source line of a rendered top-level block (including any indentation), not its ordinal. Recompute offsets against the current source after edits; keep the IDs themselves stable. Unmatched offsets are ignored: differing parser boundaries cannot shift later IDs. Missing, empty or duplicate IDs fall back to an unused `b{index}`. For duplicate offsets, the first pair wins. Nested blocks keep index keys beneath their top-level parent's key. Retained blocks spring to new positions and sizes; additions enter and removals stay mounted during their exit transition.

methods.name: style
methods.doc: Replaces the kit-derived style in [`Self::build`].

methods.name: reveal
methods.doc: Streaming word reveal in seconds (see [`El::reveal`]); 0 shows words at once.

methods.name: streaming
methods.doc: The source is still arriving: a table's last row, with no newline after it yet, is left out of the column widths until it ends, and a diagram brings in each node and edge as its line arrives. The tail draws as what it's about to become: an emphasis, strike or code span still open draws styled (never its markers), markers at the very end wait for the next character, and a trailing `| …` line waits until it's a table or isn't. Off, the text is whole.

methods.name: on_task
methods.sig: fn on_task<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, usize, bool) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called when a GFM task list item (`- [ ]` or `- [x]`) is clicked, or pressed with Space while focused: `(state, block_key, marker_offset, checked)`. Enter does not toggle. `block_key` is the top-level block's key ([`Self::block_keys`], or `b{index}`), `marker_offset` is the byte offset of `[` in the source's `[ ]`/`[x]` marker, including nested items, and `checked` is the new state. The offset refers to the source used to build this view, so the caller can replace `source[offset + 1..offset + 2]`. Without a handler, or with [`Self::tasks_read_only`], task checkboxes are read-only. Shares its slot with [`Self::on_task_tx`] (the later call wins).

methods.name: on_task_tx
methods.sig: fn on_task_tx<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, usize, bool, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: [`Self::on_task`] with the [`Tx`] of the press. Replaces any earlier `on_task` or `on_task_tx` handler (the later call wins).

methods.name: tasks_read_only
methods.doc: Keeps GFM task list checkboxes read-only (unfocusable and unpressable), even when an [`Self::on_task`] or [`Self::on_task_tx`] handler was set.

methods.name: selectable
methods.doc: Lets people select and copy the text (see [`El::selectable`]) as one selection across paragraphs, headings, list items, quotes, code blocks and table cells ([`El::selection_group`]): Cmd+A selects the whole block, and Cmd+C copies the text as drawn, laid out as plain text: a blank line around paragraphs, headings, quotes and code blocks, list items on their own lines after `- `, `1. ` or `- [ ] ` (a nested list indented past its parent's marker), and a tab between table cells, without code fences or quote marks (or the source, with [`Self::copy_source`]). Links still open on a click. The highlight is [`MarkdownStyle::selection`].

methods.name: copy_source
methods.doc: With [`Self::selectable`], copying a selection copies the Markdown source instead of the text as drawn ([`El::selection_copy`]), by whole top-level blocks: each block the selection touches, from its first line to the next block, without trailing blank lines, and the whole source verbatim when it touches every block (Cmd+A, Cmd+C). A selection inside one block that leaves part of it out (a word, a line, one list item) still copies the text as drawn.

methods.name: scroll_wide
methods.doc: Code blocks keep their lines whole and tables their columns' natural widths, each scrolling sideways in its own [`El::scroll_x`] viewport when wider than the text column, with soft left and right edges on code. Off (the default), code wraps and columns shrink.

methods.name: diagram_frame
methods.sig: fn diagram_frame(self, f: impl Fn(El, &DiagramFrame<'_>) -> El + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Draws `f(card, frame)` in place of each diagram's card, so an app can put its own controls on it (a button that opens it larger) or key it. Fences that draw as their source, or nothing yet while streaming, don't come here.  ```ignore Markdown::new(src).diagram_frame(|card, d| col().key(format!("diagram-{}", d.index)).child(card).child(open_button(d.source))) ```

methods.name: code_frame
methods.sig: fn code_frame(self, f: impl Fn(El, &CodeFrame<'_>) -> El + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Draws `f(card, frame)` in place of each code block's card, so an app can put its own controls on it (a Copy button). Diagrams that draw as their source and diff fences don't come here.  ```ignore Markdown::new(src).code_frame(|card, c| col().key(format!("code-{}", c.index)).child(card).child(copy_button(c.source))) ```

methods.name: quote_frame
methods.sig: fn quote_frame(self, f: impl Fn(El, &QuoteFrame<'_>) -> El + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Draws `f(quote, frame)` in place of each block quote, so an app can put its own controls on it (a button that copies the whole quote). Quotes inside a quote come here too.  ```ignore Markdown::new(src).quote_frame(|quote, q| col().child(quote).child(copy_button(q.text))) ```

methods.name: highlight
methods.sig: fn highlight(self, f: impl Fn(Option<&str>, &str) -> Vec<crate::syntax::Highlight> + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Colours code blocks with `f` instead of the built-in highlighter: it gets a fence's language as written (its info string's first word; `None` for an indented block or a bare fence) and the code, and returns byte ranges of the code with a token kind, which the style's [`SyntaxTheme`] colours, or a colour of its own. See [`Highlighter`] for caching, and [`syntax::builtin`](crate::syntax::builtin) to fall back on for other languages.  ```ignore Markdown::new(src).highlight(|lang, code| match lang { Some("cobol") => my_cobol(code), _ => rune_kit::syntax::builtin(lang, code), }) ```

methods.name: highlighter
methods.doc: Colours code blocks with `h` (by default [`Highlighter::builtin`]).

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Builds with `style`, for apps without a [`Kit`] (see [`MarkdownStyle::neutral`]).

types.name: MarkdownStyle
types.doc: How markdown looks. [`MarkdownStyle::from_kit`] takes every colour and font from the kit's tokens, [`MarkdownStyle::neutral`] needs no kit; each builder overrides one thing.

methods.name: link_icons
methods.sig: fn link_icons(self, size: f32, gap: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: An icon `size` points square, `gap` points before the text, ahead of every link to an `http` or `https` page: a globe in the link's colour, GitHub's mark for github.com, or the site's favicon from [`Markdown::link_favicon`]. OpenCode's markdown sets them 14 and 4. None by default.

methods.name: neutral
methods.doc: Rune's neutral light or dark look ([`Kit::neutral`]'s tokens), for apps without a kit.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: Body, heading (levels 1 to 3 and the muted level 4+) and emphasis colour.

methods.name: muted
methods.doc: Level 4+ headings and list markers.

methods.name: link
methods.doc: Link text; the underline is the same colour at 40% unless set with [`Self::link_underline`].

methods.name: inline_code_bg
methods.doc: The chip behind inline code.

methods.name: code_block
methods.sig: fn code_block(self, fill: Color, border: Color) -> Self

methods.name: code_block_padding
methods.sig: fn code_block_padding(self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: Room (x, y) inside a code block's frame; 12 by 12 by default.

methods.name: list
methods.sig: fn list(self, indent: f32, gap: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: The column a list's markers sit centred in (32 by default), and the gap between its items (4).

methods.name: quote
methods.sig: fn quote(self, rule: Color, width: f32, pad: f32, text: Color) -> Self
methods.doc: A block quote's rule, `width` points wide in `rule`, `pad` points before its text, and the text's colour (2, 12 and the body text colour by default).

methods.name: link_hover
methods.doc: The colour of a link under the pointer, underlined in it (the link colour by default).

methods.name: code_block_text
methods.doc: Code blocks' text where the highlighter leaves it uncoloured (the body text colour by default).

methods.name: plain_code_text
methods.doc: The text of plain-text code blocks: a fence with no language, or `text`, `txt`, `plain` or `plaintext` (`code_block_text`'s colour by default).

methods.name: shell_code
methods.sig: fn shell_code(self, fill: Color, border: Color, text: Color) -> Self
methods.doc: Fences in a shell language (`bash`, `sh`, `shell`, `zsh`, `fish`, `console`, `terminal`) on `fill` with a `border`, their text all in `text` with no syntax colours, as a web page that styles a command apart from code.

methods.name: list_markers_outside
methods.doc: List markers end where the item's text starts, numbers and bullets alike, as CSS's `list-style-position: outside` puts them, rather than centred in the marker column.

methods.name: list_nested_indent
methods.sig: fn list_nested_indent(self, bullets: f32, numbers: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: The marker column of a list inside a list item: `bullets` for bulleted lists and `numbers` for numbered ones (the top level's [`Self::list`] indent by default).

methods.name: task_checkbox
methods.sig: fn task_checkbox(self, size: f32, radius: f32, left: f32, top: Option<f32>, fill_on: Color, mark: Color, fill_off: Color, border_off: Color) -> Self
methods.doc: Task list checkboxes: `size` points square with corner `radius`, their left edge `left` points into the marker column and their top `top` below the item's (`None`: centred on its first line). Checked, they fill `fill_on` with a `mark` in it; unchecked, they fill `fill_off` inside a `border_off` outline. 16 points, 8 in and centred by default.

methods.name: body_font
methods.doc: Paragraphs, list items and list markers.

methods.name: heading_font
methods.sig: fn heading_font(self, level: u8, f: TextStyle) -> Self
methods.doc: The font of heading `level` (1 to 4; level 5 and deeper share 4). Level 3 sets 4 too, so a style that sets levels 1 to 3 keeps 4 and deeper in level 3's font.

methods.name: code_block_font
methods.doc: Code blocks and diffs. Inline code is set in the app's mono slot, so keep this on `Family::Mono` for the two to match; for the platform's monospaced font (SF Mono) in both, name `ui-monospace` in the mono slot of `AppSpec::families`.

methods.name: inline_code_font
methods.sig: fn inline_code_font(self, scale: f32, weight: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: Inline code's size as a multiple of the surrounding text, and its weight (the family is always the mono slot's).

methods.name: inline_code_pad

types.name: SplitView
types.doc: The app shell: `SplitView::new(main).sidebar(..).toolbar(..).inspector(..) .titlebar_inset(cx.titlebar_inset()).build(&kit)`.  The sidebar and inspector are flush panes on the window's deep background; the main pane is a rounded card beside them, inset by [`Self::frame_inset`] where no pane borders it. A 48 point band across the top is the title bar: it drags the window, its leading end clears the traffic lights (pass [`Cx::titlebar_inset`], 0 in full screen), and the sidebar's toggle button sits just past them ([`SidebarToggle`]). Panes resize from their inner edge (double-click resets the width, dragging below half the minimum collapses) and open and close together on one spring ([`PaneMotion`]). Under Reduce Motion they snap. Widths and open states live in the app's [`PaneState`]s. With [`SidebarPeek`], a closed sidebar slides in over the content while the pointer rests at the window's edge.  The band's middle is 24 points down: place the traffic lights there with `Chrome { traffic_lights: Some((16.0, 17.0)), .. }` (with [`Self::toolbar_in_panel`], the frame inset further down).  [`Cx::titlebar_inset`]: rune::Cx::titlebar_inset

types.doc: A selectable sidebar row: icon, label, then a trailing detail (a time), badge or element. `SidebarRow::new("Inbox").icon(&INBOX).badge("3").selected(sel).on_select(..).build(&kit)`. Key the built row by its item's id.  A taller row takes a second, muted line, an avatar and a status slot that turns into a close button under the pointer: `SidebarRow::new(title).height(45.0).avatar(..) .subtitle(project).status(RowStatus::Busy).on_close(..)`.

methods.name: avatar
methods.doc: A 16 point leading element in place of the icon: a project's avatar, an initial.

methods.name: subtitle
methods.sig: fn subtitle(self, s: impl Into<String>) -> Self
methods.doc: A second line under the label, smaller and fainter than it (11 point `caption` in `text_faint`, under a medium-weight 13 point label). The row's accessible name is then "Label, Subtitle". Give the row the height for it (default [`TWO_LINE_ROW_HEIGHT`]).

methods.name: title_style
methods.doc: The label's type, in place of the default (13 point; medium weight with a subtitle). It also sets the inline rename field's type.

methods.name: subtitle_style
methods.doc: The subtitle's type, in place of the default (the kit's `caption`).

methods.name: subtitle_color
methods.doc: The subtitle's colour, in place of the default (`text_faint`).

methods.name: select_only
methods.doc: A row that shows the selection but never takes focus: for a list driven from outside, such as one a search field filters and steers with its own keys. The row is out of the Tab order, Tab and Space don't act on it, and pressing it selects it (`on_select`) while a focused field stays focused (`El::preserve_focus_on_press`). Keyboard navigation of a select-only list (Up/Down and Return from the field) is the app's job. The selected row is still exposed as selected to assistive tech (`ElementInfo::item_selected`), and changing the selection never pulls focus to the row. Equivalent to `.focusable(false).focus_selected(..)` on the built row, plus the focus-preserving press.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: The row's height (default [`ROW_HEIGHT`], or [`TWO_LINE_ROW_HEIGHT`] with a subtitle).

methods.name: detail
methods.sig: fn detail(self, d: impl Into<String>) -> Self
methods.doc: Faint trailing text: a time ("2m"), a count, a shortcut.

methods.name: badge
methods.sig: fn badge(self, b: impl Into<String>) -> Self
methods.doc: A trailing pill (an unread count).

methods.name: trailing
methods.doc: Any trailing element (a status dot, a menu button), after the detail and badge.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: A 20 point slot at the row's end, after everything else.

methods.name: on_close
methods.sig: fn on_close<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: A close button in the status slot, in place of the status while the pointer is on the row. It swaps at once, with no fade.

methods.name: depth
methods.doc: Nesting level: each indents the row by [`INDENT`].

methods.name: on_select
methods.sig: fn on_select<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called when the row is pressed, or reached with the arrow keys.

methods.name: on_double_click
methods.sig: fn on_double_click<S: 'static>(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Called on a double click (rename, open in a new window).

methods.name: reorder
methods.sig: fn reorder<S: 'static>( self, state: &Reorder, index: usize, count: usize, access: fn(&mut S) -> &mut Reorder, drop: impl Fn(&mut S, usize, usize) + 'static, ) -> Self
methods.doc: Drags the row to a new place among the list's `count` rows, of which it is row `index`. It lifts above its neighbours and follows the pointer, and they step aside on springs. A drop calls `drop(s, from, to)` to move the item; Escape, or the window losing focus, puts it back. `access` finds the [`Reorder`] in the app's state. A press that doesn't move is still a select.

methods.name: renaming

methods.doc: Edits the label in place, in the field bound to `edit` (`access` finds it in the app's state). Set `edit.focused` and its text when renaming starts. Return calls `commit`, Escape calls `cancel`; both should end the rename.

methods.name: action

methods.name: shortcut

types.name: SidebarPeek
types.doc: A closed sidebar that peeks: resting the pointer on the window's leading edge, or on the sidebar's toggle, slides the sidebar in over the content as a floating surface, without moving the layout. Leaving it closes it again; pressing the toggle docks it where it is. `SplitView::sidebar_peek(SidebarPeek::new().edge(16.0, ms(40)).toggle_delay(ms(80)))`.

methods.name: new
methods.doc: A 16 point edge zone and a 12 point margin; 50 ms on the edge, 100 ms on the toggle, and 150 ms of grace before it closes; the kit's control spring.

methods.name: edge
methods.sig: fn edge(self, width: f32, delay: Duration) -> Self
methods.doc: The zone along the window's leading edge, `width` points into the content past the frame inset, and how long the pointer rests in it before the sidebar peeks.

methods.name: toggle_delay
methods.doc: How long the pointer rests on the closed sidebar's toggle before it peeks. The toggle is crossed on the way to other title bar controls, so this is usually longer than the edge's.

methods.name: below
methods.doc: Where the edge zone starts, in points from the window's top (default: below the title bar band, which holds the traffic lights and the toggle).

methods.name: hold
methods.sig: fn hold(self, margin: f32, grace: Duration) -> Self
methods.doc: How far past the sidebar and toggle the pointer may stray, and for how long, before the peek closes.

methods.name: spring
methods.doc: The spring the peek slides on (by default the kit's control spring).

methods.name: reduced_motion_fade
methods.doc: Under Reduce Motion the peek fades in place over `seconds` instead of sliding.

types.name: PaneState
types.doc: A side pane's width and whether it shows: a sidebar's or an inspector's. The app owns it (a field of its state), so it can save the width and restore it with [`PaneState::new`]. Widths are whole points within the pane's range.

methods.name: new
methods.doc: An open pane `width` points wide, which double-clicking its edge also returns to.

methods.name: range
methods.sig: fn range(self, min: f32, max: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: Its width range. The width and the default clamp into it, from the values given to [`Self::new`] and [`Self::with_width`], so `new(640.0).range(360.0, 960.0)` is 640.

methods.name: collapsed
methods.doc: Starts collapsed (a saved state, or an inspector that opens on demand).

methods.name: with_width
methods.doc: A saved width, clamped and rounded (the width it starts with; the default stays).

methods.name: is_resizing
methods.doc: Whether its edge is being dragged.

methods.name: shown_width
methods.doc: Points it takes in the layout: its width when open, else 0.

methods.name: set_width
methods.doc: Clamps to the range and rounds to a whole point. Doesn't open the pane.

methods.name: set_open
methods.doc: Opening a peeking sidebar docks it where it floats; closing ends any peek.

methods.name: is_peeking
methods.doc: Whether the closed sidebar floats over the content (a `SplitView` with [`SidebarPeek`]).

methods.name: end_peek
methods.doc: Slides a peeking sidebar away (Escape, say). Leaving it with the pointer, or the window losing focus, ends a peek too.

methods.name: peek
methods.doc: Shows the closed sidebar as a peek, over the content.

methods.name: reset_width
methods.doc: Back to the width it was made with (double-clicking its edge).

methods.name: drag_to
methods.doc: Where dragging its edge to `width` leaves it: clamped, or collapsed (keeping its last width) once dragged below half its minimum, as AppKit's split views do. Dragging back out opens it again.

types.name: PaneMotion
types.doc: How side panes open and close: `PaneMotion::new().spring(Spring::new(0.3, 0.0)) .scale_with_width(480.0, 0.15, 0.3).fade_tail(0.15)`. A `SplitView` gives both its panes the same motion, so they move as one.

methods.name: new
methods.doc: The kit's disclosure spring at every width; contents fade out early in a close and in late in an open; Reduce Motion snaps.

methods.name: spring
methods.doc: The spring a pane's width moves on (by default the kit's disclosure spring).

methods.name: scale_with_width
methods.sig: fn scale_with_width(self, reference: f32, min: f32, max: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: Scales the spring's duration by the square root of the pane's width over `reference` points, kept within `min..=max` seconds, so a narrow pane doesn't crawl and a wide one doesn't snap.

methods.name: fade_tail
methods.doc: Fades contents only across the last `fraction` of the way to closed: solid through most of a close, and there almost at once in an open.

methods.name: reduced_motion_fade
methods.doc: Under Reduce Motion the pane snaps; its contents fade over `seconds` (0 snaps them too).

methods.name: spring_for
methods.sig: fn spring_for(&self, k: &Kit, width: f32) -> Spring
methods.doc: The spring a pane `width` points wide moves on.

types.name: Toolbar
types.doc: A toolbar: `Toolbar::new().leading(..).title("..").trailing(..).build(&kit)`. The band is a window drag region (buttons in it keep their presses) and its centre slot sits in the middle of the band whatever the sides hold.

methods.name: center

methods.name: title

methods.name: material

types.name: Page

Shares [`SplitView`]'s title bar height, traffic-light clearance, window-drag band and framed content card so switching screens matches pixel for pixel: `Page::new(content).title("Settings").leading(back).trailing(done).titlebar_inset(cx.titlebar_inset()).build(&kit)`.

methods.name: title
methods.sig: fn title(self, t: impl Into<String>) -> Self
methods.doc: A centred title in the toolbar band.

methods.name: center
methods.doc: The toolbar's centre slot (replaces [`Self::title`]).

methods.name: leading
methods.doc: Adds a leading control to the toolbar (a Back button, say), placed past the traffic lights.

methods.name: trailing
methods.doc: Adds a trailing control to the toolbar.

methods.name: toolbar
methods.doc: Replaces the toolbar with a pre-built [`Toolbar`].

methods.name: titlebar_inset
methods.doc: Points the traffic lights take at the window's leading edge: `Cx::titlebar_inset`.

methods.name: past_lights
methods.sig: fn past_lights(self, past_lights: f32, edge: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: Points past the traffic lights (or the window's edge in full screen) where the toolbar's leading slot starts, matching [`SplitView::sidebar_toggle`].

methods.name: frame_inset
methods.doc: The window background showing around the content pane (default 8 points, matching [`SplitView::frame_inset`]).

methods.name: toolbar_in_panel
methods.doc: Puts the toolbar inside the framed content pane at its top, matching [`SplitView::toolbar_in_panel`].

types.name: Reorder
types.doc: A list's drag to reorder, owned by the app: `Reorder::new().gap(4.0)`. Pass it to each row's `SidebarRow::reorder`. Rows are taken to share one height.

methods.name: gap
methods.doc: Points between the rows (the list's gap), so a row steps aside by its height plus this.

methods.name: dragging

methods.name: target

components.name: TabStrip
components.summary: A strip of tabs that shrink, scroll, reorder by drag and tear out into windows. WindowTitlebar places one in the title bar.

types.name: TabStrip
types.doc: A keyed strip of tabs: `TabStrip::new("tabs", TabOrientation::Horizontal).tabs(..) .active(..).drag_state(&s.drag, |s| &mut s.drag).on_select(..).build(&kit)`.  Horizontal tabs are 28 points tall with 6 between them, share the strip from 224 points down to 28 and then scroll; a 1.5 point separator stands between neighbours that aren't active or hovered. In a `.window_drag()` titlebar the gaps between tabs, the bands above and below them and the space after the trailing action move the window, as only the tabs and buttons take presses. Vertical tabs fill the row with 3 points between them, each reaching across half the gap so no press misses.  A press selects a horizontal tab at once; a vertical one selects on release, so dragging it leaves the selection where it is ([`Self::select_on_drag_start`]). Dragging 4 points along the strip reorders, Escape puts the tab back, and with [`Self::tear_out`] dragging it off the strip tears it out. A middle click closes a tab.

methods.name: new
methods.sig: fn new(key: impl Into<String>, orientation: TabOrientation) -> Self

methods.name: tabs
methods.sig: fn tabs(self, tabs: impl IntoIterator<Item = TabItem<'a, S>>) -> Self

methods.name: active
methods.sig: fn active(self, active_id: Option<&'a str>) -> Self
methods.doc: The selected tab, by id.

methods.name: viewport_width
methods.doc: The points a horizontal strip has, trailing action included: `cx.layout_size(key)`'s width (the strip's root grows into the space it's given). It sets the tabs' shared width and density; without it they take their widest.

methods.name: zoom
methods.doc: The UI zoom the strip draws at (default 1), so drags convert from window points.

methods.name: overflow
methods.doc: The overflow policy (default [`TabOverflow::HORIZONTAL_DEFAULT`] or [`TabOverflow::VERTICAL_DEFAULT`]).

methods.name: gap
methods.doc: Points between tabs (default 6 horizontal, 3 vertical).

methods.name: row_height
methods.doc: A tab's height (default 28).

methods.name: select_on_drag_start
methods.doc: Whether a press selects the tab at once, so a drag selects it too (default true horizontal), or the release does and a drag leaves the selection (default false vertical).

methods.name: tear_out
methods.doc: Lets a drag across the strip tear a tab out ([`Self::on_tear_out`]). Off by default.

methods.name: matched_prefix
methods.sig: fn matched_prefix(self, prefix: Option<&'a str>) -> Self
methods.doc: Gives each tab `El::matched("{prefix}-{id}")`, so a tab flies between strips when the layout swaps one for another.

methods.name: reorder_spring
methods.doc: The spring tabs step aside on during a drag (default `SNAP`, 0.25 s). Drops, tabs opening and closing, and widths changing reflow on `REFLOW`.

methods.name: trailing_action
methods.doc: An element right after the last horizontal tab (the new-tab button), outside the scrolling, with the space past it left bare.

methods.name: trailing_width
methods.doc: The trailing action's width, which the tabs leave it (default 28, a large icon button).

methods.name: drag_state
methods.sig: fn drag_state(self, state: &TabDragState, access: fn(&mut S) -> &mut TabDragState) -> Self
methods.doc: The strip's gestures, kept in the app's state; `access` finds them there. Without it the tabs select and close but don't drag, and closing doesn't lock their width.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: The colour under the strip (default `bg_deep`), which a dragged tab and the close slot paint opaque.

methods.name: close_icon
methods.doc: The close button's glyph (default the kit's close glyph).

methods.name: close_tab_stop
methods.doc: Each tab's close button is a Tab stop after its tab with the kit's focus ring, as a web page's `<button>` is. Off, it's pointer only: the strip's arrows move between tabs.

methods.name: busy_indicator
methods.sig: fn busy_indicator(self, f: fn(&Kit) -> El) -> Self
methods.doc: What a busy tab shows (default the kit's spinner at 14 points).

methods.name: label
methods.sig: fn label(self, label: impl Into<String>) -> Self
methods.doc: The tab list's accessible name (default "Tabs").

methods.name: on_select
methods.sig: fn on_select(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self

methods.name: on_close
methods.sig: fn on_close(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: The close button, a middle click.

methods.name: on_double_click
methods.sig: fn on_double_click(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self

methods.name: on_hover
methods.sig: fn on_hover(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, &str, bool, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: The pointer entering (`true`) and leaving a tab.

methods.name: on_reorder
methods.sig: fn on_reorder(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, TabReorder, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self

methods.name: on_tear_out
methods.sig: fn on_tear_out(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, TabTearOut, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self

methods.name: on_tear_move
methods.sig: fn on_tear_move(self, f: impl Fn(&mut S, TabTearMove, &mut Tx) + 'static) -> Self
methods.doc: Each move of a torn-out tab, and its return to the strip, while the button is down.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: The strip. A torn-out tab stays inside the strip's clip; [`Self::build_layered`] lifts it out.

methods.name: build_layered
methods.sig: fn build_layered(self, k: &Kit, layer: &mut Vec<El>) -> El
methods.doc: The strip, with a torn-out tab floating over the window in `layer`, which the view mounts at its root with [`crate::root`] as it does popovers and menus.

types.name: TabItem
types.doc: One tab: `TabItem::new(id, title).avatar(..).status(..)`.

methods.name: new
methods.sig: fn new(id: impl Into<Cow<'a, str>>, title: impl Into<Cow<'a, str>>) -> Self

methods.name: subtitle
methods.sig: fn subtitle(self, subtitle: impl Into<Cow<'a, str>>) -> Self
methods.doc: A second, muted line under the title in a vertical strip (a project's name); the row grows to 45 points.

methods.name: avatar
methods.doc: A 16 point leading element: a project's avatar.

methods.name: icon
methods.doc: A 16 point leading icon in place of an avatar (a draft's pencil), muted until active.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Its status mark. The strip shows what it's given; OpenCode leaves the dots off the active tab and keeps the busy ring.

methods.name: pinned
methods.doc: Pinned tabs come first in the strip, keep [`TabOverflow`]'s `pinned_width` as icons, have no close button and reorder only among themselves.

methods.name: closable
methods.doc: Whether the close button and a middle click close it (default true).

methods.name: marked
methods.doc: Highlights the tab while its context menu is open.

methods.name: pulse
methods.doc: Raise it to ring a background tab once (900 ms), as a prompt arriving does.

methods.name: editor
methods.doc: A field in place of the title while renaming in place. The tab doesn't drag meanwhile.

methods.name: decorate
methods.sig: fn decorate(self, f: impl FnOnce(El, TabDensity) -> El + 'a) -> Self
methods.doc: Wraps the built tab: a context menu handler, a hover card's anchor.

types.name: TabOrientation
types.doc: Which way a [`TabStrip`] runs.

variants.name: Horizontal
variants.doc: Across a titlebar, browser style.

variants.name: Vertical
variants.doc: Down a sidebar, one tab per row.

types.name: TabDensity
types.doc: How much a horizontal tab shows, from its width ([`TabOverflow::density_for`]).

variants.name: Full
variants.doc: Over 64 points: avatar, title fading at its end, and the status or close slot.

variants.name: Compact
variants.doc: 44 to 64 points: the title hides while the tab is active, hovered or shows a status, so the slot never covers the avatar.

variants.name: IconOnly
variants.doc: 44 points or less: the avatar alone, centred, with a status dot on its corner; the close button centres over the tab under the pointer, and a busy tab spins in the avatar's place.

types.name: TabOverflow
types.doc: What a strip does when its tabs don't fit.

variants.name: ShrinkThenScroll
variants.doc: Horizontal tabs share the strip equally, from `max_width` down to `min_width`, then the strip scrolls sideways with a `fade_width` linear fade at each edge while anything is past it (Desktop's `titlebar-tabs-fade-*`). Pinned tabs keep `pinned_width`.

variants.name: Scroll
variants.doc: Full-width rows that scroll, the top and bottom feathering by as much as is left to scroll past them, up to `fade_width` (Desktop's `--vertical-tabs-fade-*`).

methods.name: tab_width
methods.sig: fn tab_width(&self, available: f32, unpinned: usize, pinned: usize, gap: f32) -> f32
methods.doc: The width of each unpinned tab when `unpinned` of them and `pinned` pinned ones share `available` points with `gap` between each: equal shares between the policy's bounds. Past the minimum the tabs overflow and the strip scrolls. `max_width` for `Scroll`.

types.name: TabItemStatus
types.doc: A tab's status mark, in the slot its close button takes under the pointer.

variants.name: Busy
variants.doc: Working: the busy indicator ([`TabStrip::busy_indicator`]), shown on the active tab too.

variants.name: Attention
variants.doc: Waiting on the user: a warning dot.

variants.name: Unread
variants.doc: Something new: an accent dot.

variants.name: Failed
variants.doc: Something new that failed: a danger dot.

types.name: TabDragState
types.doc: The gestures of one [`TabStrip`](super::TabStrip), owned by the app (`TabDragState::default()`) and passed to [`TabStrip::drag_state`](super::TabStrip::drag_state). One instance can serve a strip that moves between layouts; [`TabDragState::cancel`] drops a gesture in flight.

methods.name: phase
methods.doc: Where the gesture stands.

methods.name: dragging
methods.doc: The tab lifted by a drag (reordering or torn out), by its index.

methods.name: torn_out
methods.doc: Whether a tab is torn out of the strip.

methods.name: hovered
methods.doc: The tab under the pointer, by id.

methods.name: cancel
methods.doc: Drops a gesture in flight (a layout switch, a rename starting): the tab springs back.

methods.name: hand_off
methods.doc: The torn-out tab now shows in a window of its own that follows the pointer (on_tear_move): the strip stops drawing it until the gesture ends, or until it docks back into the strip.

methods.name: handed_off
methods.doc: Whether the torn-out tab shows in a window of its own ([Self::hand_off]).

methods.name: set_incoming
methods.doc: A tab dragged from another strip (another window's) is over this one at `point`, in this window's points, or has left it (`None`): the tabs past the slot it would land in step aside on the strip's reorder spring, as they do for a tab dragged within the strip, and close again when it leaves.

methods.name: incoming_slot
methods.doc: Where the incoming tab lands if it's let go now: the slot the strip opened its gap at, from the tabs' own lengths and the strip's scroll, as the strip last built. `None` before the strip built with it, or once it left.

types.name: WindowTitlebar
types.doc: A titlebar the app draws: leading controls, a [`TabStrip`](super::TabStrip), and trailing controls, in a `.window_drag()` band that keeps clear of the traffic lights on macOS and the caption buttons on Windows. `WindowTitlebar::from_insets(cx.chrome_insets(), zoom).leading(menu).tabs(strip).build(&kit)`.  Its buttons and tabs take their presses; the gaps between tabs, the bands above and below them and the empty stretch after the strip move the window, double-click to zoom it and, on Windows, right-click for the window menu.

methods.name: from_insets
methods.sig: fn from_insets(insets: ChromeInsets, zoom: f32) -> Self
methods.doc: Sized from the window's insets at UI zoom `zoom` (1 unscaled): the band is as tall as the window's titlebar and reserves `insets.leading / zoom` and `insets.trailing / zoom`.

methods.name: key
methods.sig: fn key(self, key: impl Into<String>) -> Self

methods.name: height
methods.doc: The band's height in points, in place of the insets'.

methods.name: top_padding
methods.doc: Points above the controls (8 on macOS, whose 28 point row sits low in a 36 point band).

methods.name: leading_padding
methods.doc: Points past the leading inset (default 14; 10 on macOS, 9 beside side tabs on Windows).

methods.name: trailing_padding
methods.doc: Points before the trailing inset (default 12).

methods.name: gap
methods.doc: Points between items (default 6).

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: The band's colour (default `bg_deep`).

methods.name: tabs
methods.doc: A horizontal strip, which takes the space between the sides. Its trailing action hugs the last tab, and the rest of its space stays bare, moving the window.

methods.name: direction
methods.doc: The direction the band sits in. Inside [`El::dir`](rune::El::dir)`(Direction::Rtl)` pass `Rtl`: its controls and tabs run from the right, while the room kept for the window's controls stays on their side (the caption buttons' on the right, the traffic lights' on the left), as Desktop's titlebar does under `dir="rtl"`. `Ltr` (the default) and `Auto` lay it out left to right.

components.name: Kit and theming
components.summary: Every component reads its colours, type, radii, motion and glyphs from a Kit. Use a theme crate, Kit::neutral, or derive one from three colours with Kit::from_palette.

methods.name: interactive
methods.doc: Gives `e` the kit's hover and press look: `c.hover` under the pointer, and `c.pressed` in its place while held, as the kit's own rows and buttons show them. `e` still needs a handler (or `.hit()`) to be hit.

methods.name: interactive_with
methods.sig: fn interactive_with(&self, e: El, hover: Color, pressed: Color) -> El
methods.doc: [`Self::interactive`] with other overlays, e.g. `c.contrast_hover` and `c.contrast_pressed` on a contrast fill. `pressed` replaces `hover` while held rather than stacking on it.

methods.name: elevate
methods.sig: fn elevate(&self, e: El, layers: &[Shadow]) -> El
methods.doc: Paints elevation layers on `e` as box shadows, e.g. `k.elevate(e, &k.elevation.floating)`.

methods.name: alpha
methods.sig: fn alpha(&self, c: Color, a: f32) -> Color
methods.doc: `c` at opacity `a`, as the browser blends it: unchanged in a window that blends in sRGB, re-solved over `blend_over` in one that blends in linear light (`rune::theme::for_blend`).

methods.name: selection
methods.doc: The text selection highlight of the kit's fields. Pass it to `El::selection_color` on `El::selectable` text so its selection looks the same.

methods.name: on
methods.sig: fn on(&self, c: Color, backdrop: Color) -> Color
methods.doc: A straight-alpha colour as painted on `backdrop`: re-solved for that surface when the window blends in linear light, unchanged when it blends in sRGB.

methods.name: shadow_layers
methods.sig: fn shadow_layers<'a>(&'a self, layers: &'a [Shadow]) -> impl Iterator<Item = Shadow> + 'a
methods.doc: `layers` as painted: rings recoloured by [`Kit::ring`] when the theme sets it.

methods.name: light_on
methods.sig: fn light_on(&self, a: f32, backdrop: Color) -> Color
methods.doc: White at opacity `a` painted on `backdrop`.

methods.name: light
methods.doc: White at opacity `a` (the `alpha-light-*` ramp).

methods.name: dark_a
methods.doc: Black at opacity `a` (the `alpha-dark-*` ramp).

methods.name: scroll_bar
methods.doc: Wraps `viewport` (an [`El::scroll`](rune::El::scroll) element) with a vertical scroll bar over its right edge that follows the system "Show scroll bars" preference and rides scroll offsets through live values with zero view rebuilds per scroll frame.

methods.name: from_palette
methods.doc: Derives surfaces, text, borders, states and elevation from three theme colours. Appearance is dark when `fg` is lighter than `bg`.  - Layers step OKLab lightness away from `bg` (+0.04, then +0.03 per elevation when dark; smaller steps the other way when light). Dark surfaces step from at least #0a0a0a's lightness, so pure black still gets visible layers and status tints. - Derived neutrals (layers, opaque borders, secondary text) keep the hue and chroma of the more colourful of `bg` and `fg`, so warm palettes stay warm. - `border_muted`/`border_base`/`border_strong`, hover and press are `fg` at low alpha, as a browser blends it: authored for sRGB blending, and solved over `bg` (`blend_over`) when the kit is built in a window that blends in linear light. Opaque `std_border`/`border_*` tokens are lightness steps. - Secondary text mixes towards `fg` in OKLab, with contrast floors of 4.5:1 (muted) and 3:1 (faint) when `fg` supports them. - Focus rings are a neutral blue, not `accent`; [`Kit::from_palette_focus`] picks accent, ink or a custom colour instead. - Elevation rings are `c.border_base`, and re-resolve when painted (`Kit::ring`), so overriding it restyles them.  ``` use rune::{Color, color::hex}; use rune_kit::{Kit, PaletteSeed}; let kit = Kit::from_palette(PaletteSeed { bg: Color::BLACK, fg: Color::WHITE, accent: hex("#e53935").unwrap(), }); ```

methods.name: from_palette_focus
methods.sig: fn from_palette_focus(seed: PaletteSeed, focus: PaletteFocus) -> Kit
methods.doc: [`Kit::from_palette`] with the focus ring from `focus`.  ``` use rune::Color; use rune_kit::{Kit, PaletteFocus, PaletteSeed}; let seed = PaletteSeed { bg: Color::BLACK, fg: Color::WHITE, accent: Color::WHITE }; let kit = Kit::from_palette_focus(seed, PaletteFocus::Ink); assert_eq!(kit.c.border_focus, Color::WHITE); ```

types.name: PaletteSeed
types.doc: Three opaque theme colours from which [`Kit::from_palette`] derives its semantic tokens. Typography, radii, motion and individual colours remain editable on the resulting kit.

types.name: PaletteFocus
types.doc: Where [`Kit::from_palette_focus`] takes the focus-ring colour from.

variants.name: Blue
variants.doc: A neutral blue that reads as focus on any palette.

variants.name: Accent
variants.doc: The seed's accent.

variants.name: Ink
variants.doc: The seed's foreground (text) colour.

variants.name: Custom
variants.doc: This colour. `Custom(cx.focus_color())` follows the user's system accent, as AppKit's rings do.

types.name: Palette
types.doc: Semantic colours. Translucent tokens are resolved for the blend mode of the window the kit was built for (`rune::theme::blends_srgb`): as authored when it blends in sRGB, the default, and solved over [`Kit::blend_over`] when it blends in linear light (see `rune::theme::for_blend`). Hashable, as [`Type`] and [`Radius`] are, so a row can use the tokens it reads as a `memo` version.

types.name: Elevation
types.doc: Elevation tokens as box-shadow layers (outer and inset), painted in order. Build one from [`Elevation::default`], setting its fields, and [`Elevation::with_input`] for the fields'.

methods.name: with_input
methods.sig: fn with_input(self, layers: impl Into<Vec<Shadow>>) -> Self
methods.doc: Text fields' and field selects' own shadow, `--v2-elevation-input`: in OpenCode's dark theme lighter than a button's (no drop, a 16% light ring). Without it fields take [`Self::button_neutral`].

methods.name: input
methods.doc: The shadow text fields and field selects draw ([`Self::with_input`]).

types.name: Type
types.doc: The type scale. Sizes, weights, line heights and tracking in points.

methods.name: caption
methods.doc: Secondary text under a control or row (a setting's explanation, a file's size): `small` on a 16 line, so 11 / 16 in the built-in themes. A method rather than a field, so a theme's own `Type` gets it from its `small`.

types.name: Motion
types.doc: Motion tokens. Hover/press overlays use the runtime's own snappy track.

types.name: State
types.doc: `Gliding` is an eased zoom under way, stepped from the frame clock since `last`. A press doesn't stop a glide, so a double-click's third click leaves it running; the hand moving does.

types.name: ControlSize
types.doc: A control's size, named and measured as AppKit's `NSControl.ControlSize` on macOS 27. A push button is 16, 20, 24, 28 or 36 points tall; a switch's track 16, 20, 24, 28 or 36.
